# Ring Mood

**Ring Modulator with Selectable Modulator Sources**

A VST3 effect for Windows. The input is multiplied by a modulator you choose: a band
limited oscillator, filtered noise, the signal itself, or a sidechain input. Written in
C++20 on JUCE.

![Ring Mood main window](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ClyntiaAikaHanaa/Ring-Mood/HEAD/Screenshot/Main.png)

## What it does

Ring modulation multiplies two signals together. What comes out is not the two inputs but
their sum and difference frequencies, which is why the effect sounds metallic and
inharmonic rather than simply brighter. It is one of the oldest tricks in electronic
music and still one of the fastest ways to make a sound stop being acoustic.

Most ring modulators give you one sine oscillator and stop there. Ring Mood keeps the
control set just as small, five knobs and one selector, but lets the modulator itself be
something other than a sine: a saw or square for harder, buzzier products, filtered noise
for pitched grit, the input signal for self modulation, or an external track through the
sidechain.

Three things shape the design:

1. **One screen, no pages.** Five knobs, one selector, one display. Everything the plugin
   can do is visible at once.
2. **Zero latency.** The whole path is one multiply per sample. There is no lookahead and
   no oversampling, so it stays usable while tracking and on the master bus.
3. **The display shows the truth.** The preview draws the finished modulator, after
   Rectify and Bias, which is the exact number the input is multiplied by. It cannot drift
   from what you hear.

## Features

### Engine

* Sample by sample multiply, no added latency and no reported latency.
* Sine, saw and square oscillators. Saw and square are corrected with PolyBLEP at their
  discontinuities, so a 5 kHz square does not fold a wall of aliases into the sum and
  difference tones the effect is there to produce.
* Band pass noise from a TPT state variable filter at high Q, so the noise reads as
  pitched at the Freq. setting instead of as a wash.
* Peak follower on the noise source, which keeps modulation depth even across the whole
  Freq. range. A fixed makeup gain would be silent at one end and clipped at the other.
* All parameters are smoothed over 8 ms, so automation jumps and mode switches cannot
  click.

### Modulator sources

| Source | What modulates the input |
| --- | --- |
| Sine oscillator | Internal sine at Freq. |
| Saw oscillator | Band limited saw at Freq. |
| Square oscillator | Band limited square at Freq. |
| Band pass noise | White noise through a narrow band pass centred on Freq. |
| Self | The input signal itself, for self ring modulation |
| Sidechain | The second stereo input bus, for modulating one track with another |

### Shaping

* **Bias** slides the modulator off zero. At 0 percent it is bipolar and you get true ring
  modulation. Towards either extreme it becomes unipolar and the effect turns into
  tremolo or amplitude modulation. The result is renormalised, so raising Bias changes the
  character without also raising the level.
* **Rectify** blends towards the full wave rectified shape, which adds harmonics and
  effectively doubles the modulator rate at the top of the range.
* **Mix** crossfades dry against the modulated signal.

### Stereo

* **Spread** reads one oscillator at two phase offsets rather than running two detuned
  copies, up to a quarter turn either side. That makes it reversible: winding Spread back
  to 0 percent puts both channels exactly back in phase, with no accumulated offset left
  behind.
* 100 percent lands on quadrature rather than a half turn. A half turn would be wider on
  paper, but it makes the channels exact inverses, so the wet signal would vanish the
  moment anything summed it to mono.
* Band pass noise spreads by detuning the two filter centres instead. A filter has no
  phase to accumulate, so there it really is a frequency difference.

### Interface

* Preview of the finished modulator at 30 fps, filled for the left channel with the right
  channel as a hairline. The two separate only once Spread is up.
* The window spans a fixed number of modulator cycles, so the trace stays readable at
  1 Hz and at 5 kHz alike.
* Freq. and Spread dim automatically in Self and Sidechain, where they do nothing.
* Double click any knob to return it to its default.
* Resizable from 75 percent to 200 percent with the whole layout scaled as one unit.	

## Sidechain routing

The Sidechain source reads a second stereo input bus, which is disabled by default so
hosts that cannot route it still load the plugin as an ordinary stereo insert. Enable and
route that bus in the host, then pick Sidechain in the selector. When the bus is not
connected the mode outputs silence rather than quietly falling back to something else,
which makes an unrouted sidechain obvious instead of confusing.

## Project layout

```
Source/
  RingMoodDSP.h     oscillators, state variable filter, noise, shaping helpers
  Params.*          parameter layout, ranges, modulator mode list
  PluginProcessor.* audio path, buses, state, modulator scope
  PluginEditor.*    fixed size canvas, scaled by a single transform
  MainPanel.*       layout and painting of the whole face
  WaveDisplay.*     modulator preview
  Widgets.h         arc knob, modulator pill, menu look and feel, brand mark
  RingMoodTheme.h   palette, fonts, shared dimensions
Tools/
  logoexport.cpp    brand asset export
Screenshot/
  Main.png
  Logo.png
  make_logo.ps1
```

The editor never asks how large the window is. `MainPanel` is always laid out at its design
size of 620 by 560 and the editor applies one affine scale to it, with the aspect ratio
locked by the constrainer. Every knob, font, corner radius and gap therefore moves at
exactly the same rate when the window is dragged, and no element carries size logic of its
own. The last size is stored with the parameters, so the editor reopens where you left it.
